period: Chalcolithic; Iron II (7th c. BCE); Roman (contemporary with Khirbet Qumran); visits c. 10th c. CE and 18th/19th c.
quote: Elle ouvre au sud-est, surplombe d'une vingtaine de mètres en pente douce le cheminement
notes: Grid printed as 'entrance point according to the Israeli Grid' (survey G. Levi, Mabat 3D, March 2017); values are in the new-grid range. Length 19 m = dimension '1900cm' printed on the 2017 section (Fig. 6, p. 76; vertical extent printed 500 cm). Height 2 m = 'vide à peu près uniforme de deux mètres de hauteur' (p. 46). Plan-scaled for comparison: 2017 Fig. 1 (p. 72) extents c. 21.5 m (entrance to NW end) x c. 17 m; ch. 2 Fig. 6 mouth to back (h) c. 15 m, to end of gallery g c. 19.5 m. Location: c. 1.5 km N of Khirbet Qumran and 500 m N of Cave 1Q (p. 1); 'presque 2 km au nord du Khirbet, un peu au sud de la Grotte 3' (de Vaux 1956, p. 22); Cave 3Q 300 m N of 11Q (p. 71 n. 2); Patrich's cave 24 50 m N (p. 63); in the lowest ledge of the cliff, c. 20 m above the path 150 m away at the cliff foot (p. 46); Harding: 'some 50 feet up the scarp' (p. 23). Natural karst cavity from dissolution of a stratum; ceiling one slab tilted to the south (p. 46); single natural pillar divides two chambers (p. 67). One entrance; a well-like crevice above the back (h) was thought a second entrance but 'n'a pu être un passage' (p. 52), so not counted. Largest of the natural manuscript caves (p. 71). Entrance found blocked in 1956. Other caves named here (1Q, 3Q, A, B, Patrich 24) not keyed.

period: Chalcolithic; Iron II (7th c. BCE); Roman (contemporary with Khirbet Qumran)
quote: The doorway, once cleared, is 1.60 meters wide, 1.35 meters high, to the Roman floor
notes: De Vaux field notes 1 Mar 1956 (p. 17 French, p. 19 translation); repeated pp. 52, 78. These are the dimensions of the opening as widened by de Vaux (26-27 Feb 1956); the ancient access was narrower and lower (p. 48). 'L'entrée reconnue de 11Q s'ouvre au sud-est' (p. 48). Grid point is this entrance. Opens on a vertical fracture striking N 150°, conjugate with a N 30° ceiling fracture (Massonnat p. 67). Today the mouth is wide open ('béante', p. 52); on 2017 Fig. 1 the mouth between rock walls is c. 9 m, fronted by blocks A and B (plan-scaled, note only). Harding: entrance collapsed anciently, leaving only a very small hole (p. 23).

quote: Le blocage a vraisemblablement été construit par ceux qui, ayant caché des manuscrits
notes: Large collapsed blocks of rock/pudding stone in front of the entrance under the clandestine diggers' debris (diary 26 Feb 1956); partly removed by de Vaux. Humbert: built by those who hid the scrolls; two stones between vault and fill may be its base (pp. 48, 52, 61-62). 2017 notes: blockage explicable by natural processes, human contribution not excluded (p. 73). Construction therefore 'unknown'.

quote: Block A to the west collapsed from the ceiling above the entrance
notes: One of two large conglomerate blocks in front of the entrance. Size plan-scaled on 2017 Fig. 1 (scale bar 0-3 m, 1 m grid). Fine sediment accumulated between A and the entrance; a long narrow breach runs behind A (p. 73).

quote: the eastern block lying farther away (about 1 m) from the entrance
notes: Originated from the cliff-side orthogonal to the entrance; to the east. Its advanced position redirects some overflow water into the cave (p. 73). Size plan-scaled on 2017 Fig. 1.

quote: Behind block A, a long, narrow breach runs from the ceiling to the bottom
notes: Shown in 2017 Figs 9-10; taken as a model of how the whole entrance area may have looked before 1956.

period: Chalcolithic; Iron II (7th c. BCE); Roman (contemporary with Khirbet Qumran)
quote: Elle comprend une première chambre circulaire
notes: Plan-scaled on ch. 2 Fig. 6 (scale bar 0-18 m; north arrow taken as pointing to page right, which matches the text's SE-facing entrance). Extents of the standing-height zone: c. 6.5 m N-S x 6.6 m E-W (area c. 23 m2). Openings: entrance a (bearing c. 115°, SE), passage l to c (c. 19°, N), access to d (c. 290°, W/NW boundary); recess e not counted. Fill: yellow water-laid earth c. 50 cm over ashy Chalcolithic floor on rock; 54 cm between Chalcolithic and Roman levels; NE sediment remnant almost 1 m thick (pp. 17-19, 55, 59). Cache authors could barely stand here (p. 51). 2017 Operation B (two 1.80 x 1.80 m squares) dug here (p. 78), not keyed.

period: Chalcolithic; Iron II (7th c. BCE); Roman (contemporary with Khirbet Qumran)
quote: se courber sous le plafond bas en (l) pour passer de (b) en (c)
notes: Plan-scaled on ch. 2 Fig. 6 (scale bar 0-18 m; north arrow taken as pointing to page right, which matches the text's SE-facing entrance). Zone of lowered vault between b and c: c. 3 m across (between w and v) and c. 3 m deep (b to c). A large portion of ceiling collapsed here in geological times; floor rises from b to c. Humbert reconstructs a door through partition v-w here (p. 64).

period: Chalcolithic; Iron II (7th c. BCE); Roman (contemporary with Khirbet Qumran)
quote: à l'arrière de laquelle s'ouvre une grande chambre dont le sol rocheux monte rapidement
notes: Plan-scaled on ch. 2 Fig. 6 (scale bar 0-18 m; north arrow taken as pointing to page right, which matches the text's SE-facing entrance). 8.5 m = from passage l to the back (h), including the low-vault zone; standing-height zone c. 4.8 x 7.0 m (c. 22 m2). Openings: l to b (c. 176°, S), awkward step to d (c. 253°, W). Floor rises steeply; raised bench j; back (h) is a loose-earth slope where the rock ceiling ends in an overhang (p. 52). Humbert: the scrolls were deposited here, just right of passage l ('dépôt' on Fig. 6). Filled with bat guano in 1956. The 2017 vertical passage to the upper chamber lies in the cave's 'northern corner'; the source does not say it opens from c, so not counted.

class_as_printed: salle (d), seconde chambre de la grotte intérieure
quote: nous considérons cette dernière comme la seconde chambre de la grotte intérieure
notes: Plan-scaled on ch. 2 Fig. 6 (scale bar 0-18 m; north arrow taken as pointing to page right, which matches the text's SE-facing entrance). Bounding extents of the standing-height zone c. 6.0 m N-S x 4.4 m E-W (area c. 13 m2); the text calls it 'exiguë'. Openings: to b (c. 159°, S/SE boundary), to c (c. 42°, NE), narrow low passage to gallery f (c. 233°, SW). Floor lower than b and c; block q lies in it; facing x on its south side. At Qumran time only b and c were easily usable (p. 51).

quote: Dans une fracture du banc supérieur ... qui rejoint le diverticule (e)
notes: Plan-scaled on ch. 2 Fig. 6 (scale bar 0-18 m; north arrow taken as pointing to page right, which matches the text's SE-facing entrance). Recess off b on its east side (c. 67° from the centre of b). A fracture seen on the façade above right of the entrance joins it; strong infiltration (p. 59). Its mouth faces b at c. 247° (W/SW boundary), so direction left blank. Possibly Patrich's 'crevice to the right of the entrance' (not stated).

quote: On arrête le travail dans la galerie, qui s'enfonce à gauche
notes: Plan-scaled on ch. 2 Fig. 6 (scale bar 0-18 m; north arrow taken as pointing to page right, which matches the text's SE-facing entrance). Length from the edge of d to the end of g. Dead-end corridor narrowing ('étroiture f-g'), very low ceiling, full of large stones; one moves bent, then on knees; ceiling lowers to meet a soil layer (pp. 48, 51). De Vaux stopped work here 13 Mar 1956: dangerous, 'il n'y avait d'ailleurs rien'. Its one mouth opens to d (c. 101°, E).

quote: pour observer l'élargissement (g), dans lequel on hésite à s'engager tant il est bas
notes: Widening at the end of gallery f; extent not defined on the plan, so no size keyed.

quote: la banquette (j) surélevée en équerre, large et impropre à la déambulation
notes: Raised L-shaped bench in c; shown as a low-vault zone along the west and north sides of c on Fig. 6. Construction not stated; extent not measurable.

quote: un reste de maçonnerie dans l'anfractuosité (k) : le creux du rocher va en s'amincissant
notes: Rock recess on the south wall at the west end of the dashed arc; masonry u hooked into it.

quote: La salle (d) est encombrée d'un gros quartier (q) détaché du plafond
notes: Plan-scaled on ch. 2 Fig. 6 (scale bar 0-18 m; north arrow taken as pointing to page right, which matches the text's SE-facing entrance). Fallen ceiling block, deeply embedded in the rubble, fallen before historical times.

class_as_printed: témoin géologique en forme de pilier (r); pilier naturel; "pillar"
quote: La cavité est séparée en deux chambres par un pilier naturel vierge de toute karstification
notes: Plan-scaled on ch. 2 Fig. 6 (scale bar 0-18 m; north arrow taken as pointing to page right, which matches the text's SE-facing entrance). On 2017 Fig. 1 it is 'X', c. 2 x 2 m. The cave is organised around it (p. 51); separates entrance chamber from back chamber (Massonnat, p. 67, Fig. 7); connects ceiling and ground; the 'arch' seems sustained by it but it is not aligned with the arch axis (p. 82). Masonry v built against it.

quote: forming a sort of "arch" spanning through the cave's width
notes: Rock layer in the middle of the cave between inner and outer parts. Length = span of the stippled 'arch' band across the cave on 2017 Fig. 1 (scale bar 0-3 m, 1 m grid).

quote: a remarkable wedge behind the "arch", to the left of the "pillar"
notes: Rock wedge detaching from the core along NW-SE sub-vertical faults. Size plan-scaled on 2017 Fig. 1.

quote: A fallen conglomerate slab is also visible to the right of entrance hall.
notes: 'Entrance hall' taken as b.

quote: la construction put accrocher la cloison (u-v) à la paroi sud
notes: Plan-scaled on ch. 2 Fig. 6 (scale bar 0-18 m; north arrow taken as pointing to page right, which matches the text's SE-facing entrance). Masonry remnant in recess k; anchored partition u-v to the south wall. Known only from 1956 photographs; not mentioned by de Vaux; dismantled before Patrich's 1988 work (pp. 57, 63-64, 82). Humbert dates the masonry to the Chalcolithic; the 2017 notes suggest the 1956 excavators built such walls as supports (p. 85).

quote: érigée avec soin, sans assises, les blocs imbriqués les uns dans les autres
notes: Plan-scaled on ch. 2 Fig. 6 (scale bar 0-18 m; north arrow taken as pointing to page right, which matches the text's SE-facing entrance). Best preserved; dry stone; rested on rock per photographs, yet 'ne s'enfonce pas plus bas que' the Roman floor (p. 64). Known only from 1956 photographs; not mentioned by de Vaux; dismantled before Patrich's 1988 work (pp. 57, 63-64, 82). Humbert dates the masonry to the Chalcolithic; the 2017 notes suggest the 1956 excavators built such walls as supports (p. 85).

quote: surmonté d'une maçonnerie (w) de plusieurs pierres
notes: Plan-scaled on ch. 2 Fig. 6 (scale bar 0-18 m; north arrow taken as pointing to page right, which matches the text's SE-facing entrance). Several stones on top of a large block standing like a door-jamb at the entrance to the inner cave; part of partition v-w; now dismantled (p. 55). Known only from 1956 photographs; not mentioned by de Vaux; dismantled before Patrich's 1988 work (pp. 57, 63-64, 82). Humbert dates the masonry to the Chalcolithic; the 2017 notes suggest the 1956 excavators built such walls as supports (p. 85).

quote: au moins un parement (x) qui rectifie la paroi au sud
notes: Plan-scaled on ch. 2 Fig. 6 (scale bar 0-18 m; north arrow taken as pointing to page right, which matches the text's SE-facing entrance).
